words.intro: Program a real rover: write the moves, steer around craters, and rescue a stranded probe **before the battery runs out**.
words.finished: Five missions, all driven by your code. Mission control is proud.
words.tinker: Keep tinkering: write your own functions, like turn_around() or drive(squares), and try to finish with even more battery.

milestones.title: First drive
milestones.goal: The rover rolls to the flag.

steps.instruction: Mission 1! The flag is on the same row as the rover. What happens with `rover.forward(2)`?
choices: It drives 2 squares and stops before the flag
steps.explain: `rover.forward(2)` drives exactly 2 squares. The flag is 4 squares away, so the rover stops short. Robots do *exactly* what you say!
hints: Count the squares between the rover and the flag.
The number in `forward(...)` is how many squares it drives.
`rover.forward(1)` drives one square.
The flag is __ squares away, but the code says 2.
It drives 2 squares and stops before the flag. Pick that and Run.

steps.instruction: Change the number so the rover stops **right on the flag**.
hints: Only the number in `rover.forward(...)` needs to change.
Count the squares from the rover to the flag on the stage.
If the flag were 3 squares away, you'd write `rover.forward(3)`.
`rover.forward(_)`
`rover.forward(4)`.

milestones.title: Turn the corner
milestones.goal: The rover turns to reach a flag up the map.

steps.instruction: Mission 2: the flag is **up** the map. After `forward(4)`, add `rover.turn("left")`, then drive forward to the flag.
hints: Add 2 lines at the bottom: a turn and a forward.
`rover.turn("left")` makes a quarter turn. Then the rover faces up the map.
`rover.turn("right")` then `rover.forward(2)` would turn and drive 2 squares down.
`rover.turn("left")` then `rover.forward(_)`
Add `rover.turn("left")` and `rover.forward(3)`.

steps.instruction: Think like a rover. It faces right, then does `turn("left")` **twice**. Which way is it facing now?
steps.explain: Each turn is a quarter turn. Two quarter turns make a half turn: a U-turn. Now it faces the opposite way.
hints: Try it with your own body: face the screen, turn left, turn left again.
One turn is a quarter of a full spin.
Two quarters make a half.
A half turn faces the ________ way.
Left. It did a U-turn.

milestones.title: Dodge craters
milestones.goal: A go_around() function that steers past craters.

steps.instruction: Mission 3: a crater blocks the way! Steer around it: turn left, forward 1, turn right, forward 2, turn right, forward 1, turn left… then on to the flag.
hints: The rover is just before the crater. Plan the route square by square with your finger.
To go around: step to the side, drive past, step back. Each step is a turn plus a forward.
`rover.turn("left")` then `rover.forward(1)` moves the rover up one row.
Left, forward(1), right, forward(2), right, forward(1), left, then forward(_) to the flag.
Add: `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(1)`, `rover.turn("right")`, `rover.forward(2)`, `rover.turn("right")`, `rover.forward(1)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(2)`.

steps.instruction: Mission 4 has **three** craters. Writing those 7 moves three times is boring, so they're in a **function** called `go_around()`. Fill the blank to dodge the middle crater.
hints: The blank is between two `rover.forward(1)` lines.
`def go_around():` only describes the moves. Writing `go_around()` runs them.
The first crater is dodged by the line `go_around()` near the bottom.
Replace `___` with `go_around()`.

steps.instruction: Still repeating! Replace the repeated lines with a loop: keep the first `rover.forward(1)`, then `for crater in range(3):` with `go_around()` and `rover.forward(1)` pushed in underneath.

check.description: Short code, same mission. That's what programmers love.

hints: The pattern `go_around()` then `rover.forward(1)` happens 3 times.
A for loop repeats the pushed-in lines. `range(3)` means 3 times.
`for i in range(3):` then `    print("hi")` prints hi three times.
`rover.forward(1)`, then `for crater in range(3):`, then `    go_around()` and `    rover.forward(_)`.
After the function, write only: `rover.forward(1)` / `for crater in range(3):` / `    go_around()` / `    rover.forward(1)`.

milestones.title: Rescue the probe
milestones.goal: Pick up the probe and get home before the battery dies.

steps.instruction: Final mission! Drive to the **probe**, pick it up, and bring the rover **back to base**. Plan your route around the craters. Watch the battery!

check.description: Rescue complete! The probe is safe.

hints: Plan first: trace a route on the stage with your finger, avoiding every crater.
The bottom row and the top row have no craters at all.
Start with `rover.turn("right")` and `rover.forward(1)` to reach the bottom row.
Bottom row out: right, forward(1), left, forward(7), left, forward(4). Then home: forward(1), left, forward(_), left, forward(4).

`rover.turn("right")`, `rover.forward(1)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(7)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(4)`, `rover.forward(1)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(7)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(4)`.

steps.instruction: Mission control's challenge: finish the rescue with **at least 22%** battery left. Fewer squares and fewer turns save power.

check.description: New battery record! Mission control is cheering.

hints: Every square costs 3% and every turn costs 1%. Count your route's cost.
Turning around (two turns) costs 2%. Is there a route home that doesn't need it?
Going out along the bottom row and home along the top row needs only 5 turns in total.
After the probe, keep facing up: forward(1), left, forward(7), left, forward(_).

`rover.turn("right")`, `rover.forward(1)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(7)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(5)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(7)`, `rover.turn("left")`, `rover.forward(4)`.
